codeReview.summary: The redesign updated the light-mode bubble/chip/composer shapes, but it does not fully match the Cellar Ledger spec. The committed components use the wrong border token for all assistant surfaces, and they also rely on `surfaceVariant` for dark-mode card backgrounds even though that token maps to the darker hover surface instead of the wireframed card color.

issues.description: Assistant/loading bubbles use `m3.colorScheme.outlineVariant` for their 1px border here, and the same mistake appears in `src/components/assistant/SuggestionChips.tsx:57` and `src/components/assistant/InputBar.tsx:76,186`. In `src/styles/theme.ts:404`, `outlineVariant` resolves to `surface[200]` (`#EEE7DD` light / `#242A24` dark), but VAL-AI-002/003 and the wireframes require the stone-3/card-border token (`#D9D0C4` / `#2E342F`). The assistant UI therefore ships the wrong border color in both themes.

Assistant bubbles use `m3.colorScheme.surfaceVariant` here, and the same background token is reused in `src/components/assistant/SuggestionChips.tsx:56` and `src/components/assistant/InputBar.tsx:67-68,184`. In `src/styles/theme.ts:400`, dark `surfaceVariant` maps to `surface[200]` (`#242A24`), but the dark AI-assistant wireframe specifies `bg-card`/mist-1 (`#1A1E1B`) for assistant bubbles, suggestion chips, and the input bar. Dark mode therefore does not match the required bark-charcoal card surfaces.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared docs do not explicitly map which M3 semantic roles correspond to Cellar Ledger card and border tokens, which made it easy to pick `surfaceVariant`/`outlineVariant` even though those resolve to the wrong dark-mode surfaces.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `src/styles/theme.ts:400-404` maps `surfaceVariant` to `surface[200]` and `outlineVariant` to `surface[200]`, while the dark wireframe uses `bg-card` `#1A1E1B` and `border` `#2E342F` for the assistant surfaces. The feature code follows the misleading M3 names in `MessageBubble.tsx`, `SuggestionChips.tsx`, and `InputBar.tsx`.
